At `3ac246c8b497f4c560d75b1465aeab54ceb78494`, the requested lifecycle exists in Rust. Its supported contract is narrower than unrestricted production operation: **GC requires single-host quiescence, budgets model payload rather than total RSS, and some growth requires explicit profile selection.**

All locations below refer to that commit. Tests listed are **source-authored coverage, not executed qualification**.

| Capability | Public API and implementation evidence | Authored test evidence / limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Incremental insert/update/delete | `apply_two_bit_mutations`; signed IDs, upsert vectors and delete tombstones. Sorted unique batches, bounded snapshots and CAS publication: [mutations:380](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/src/two_bit_mutations.rs:380). | Mutation, stale-writer and lost-ack assertions: [application_ids:315](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/tests/two_bit_application_ids.rs:315). Each batch rewrites the bounded pending snapshot. |
| Authenticated publication and pinned reads | `publish_two_bit_generation`, `read_two_bit_head`, `TwoBitIndex::open_remote/open_coordinated/search`: [store:1501](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/src/two_bit_store.rs:1501), [index:31](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/src/two_bit_index.rs:31). Immutable hashes, conditional control updates and range authentication. Store ACLs establish writer authority. | Corruption/budget coverage: [generation test:2371](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/tests/two_bit_generation.rs:2371). Low-level publication requires the caller to preserve corpus contents; compaction additionally validates prepared IDs and vectors. |
| Restart/recovery | `read_two_bit_mutations`, `recover_two_bit_source`, durable compaction job/ready records: [mutations:297](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/src/two_bit_mutations.rs:297), [compaction:717](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/src/two_bit_compaction.rs:717). | Ready-publication recovery: [application_ids:3077](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/tests/two_bit_application_ids.rs:3077); multiple interruption phases: [3214](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/tests/two_bit_application_ids.rs:3214). Its background maintenance does not establish automatic maintenance for `TwoBitIndex`. |

Three simulated perspectives expose concrete release gates; these are analytical viewpoints, not expert testimony:

| Perspective and predicted failure | Source-checkable gate | One bounded next test |
|---|---|---|
| **Operations:** repeated bounded GC calls may never reach garbage. | Every call restarts listing; retained/unknown objects consume the scan budget: [gc:219](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/src/two_bit_gc.rs:219). This blocks a guarantee of eventual reclamation under a fixed scan cap. | Ordered disposable store: four unknown keys before one recognized orphan; scan cap four; three passes. Expected counterexample: zero deletions and `scan_complete=false` each time. |
| **Storage engine:** ordinary growth can leave writes sealed after compaction rejects. | Preflight clamps the modeled row count, then seals; actual geometry admission happens later: [compaction:652](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/src/two_bit_compaction.rs:652), [840](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/src/two_bit_compaction.rs:840). The authored 100,001-row case explicitly asserts the sealed state. Explicit Scale1m recovery exists. | Run only [the existing D2 boundary test](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/tests/two_bit_application_ids.rs:3689), then verify a new mutation succeeds after explicit Scale1m recovery. This gates unattended growth across Native100k’s limit—not data integrity. |
| **Distributed systems:** a pinned reader outside the shared directory can lose backing objects. | Reader registration is local; GC retains current data only: [index:26](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/src/two_bit_index.rs:26), [gc:171](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/src/two_bit_gc.rs:171). This blocks multi-host reader-safe GC claims. | Two small generations and two maintenance directories: retain an old reader, publish replacement, GC through the other directory, query the old reader. Control case: the same directory must reject GC before deletion. |

**Actionable plan:** qualify the existing single-host lifecycle first. Run those three targeted falsifiers on an authorized bounded lane; resolve GC progress, establish the profile-transition contract, and enforce one shared maintenance directory. Then run one small insert → update/delete → interrupted compaction → restart → GC → refill lifecycle with measured RSS, scratch and concurrency limits. Keep `Fresh1m` outside the mutable release envelope unless explicitly transitioned. The native S3 smoke is authored but ignored by default at [application_ids:2025](/home/rb/git/borsuk/crates/borsuk/tests/two_bit_application_ids.rs:2025); its existence is not S3 qualification.

Skipped all edits, builds, tests, network/AWS access and scientific artifacts; the remote comparison remained untouched.  
Risk: source coverage does not establish crash durability, real-store semantics or total-process resource compliance.
